Summary adjusted using the Financial Stability Report (FSR):
- Policy stance: The FOMC kept the federal funds rate at 0–0.25% and continued asset purchases ($80B Treasuries, $40B agency MBS) with strong forward guidance, consistent with average-inflation-targeting to re-anchor expectations at 2% while supporting recovery.
- Macro backdrop: Vaccinations and policy support are strengthening activity and employment; inflation has picked up but is described as largely transitory. The outlook remains tied to the course of the virus.
- FSR lens on risks/conditions: The FSR notes overall accommodative financial conditions but highlights elevated vulnerabilities—stretched asset valuations, lingering fragilities in short-term dollar funding markets, and sectoral exposures amplified by the pandemic. While bank capital/liquidity are solid and policy backstops support credit, downside risks from a pandemic resurgence and rapid shifts in risk appetite remain.
- Net tone: Positive on growth momentum and policy support, but tempered by elevated financial stability vulnerabilities flagged in the FSR.
